mutants.reason: mubi4_test_false_loose is only called inside assertions in prim_alert_receiver. It drives no logic and no port, so the change is unobservable.

op_get is inverted, so the 'PutFullData must set all active lanes' check (fulldata_chk) is skipped for PutFullData, and a Get with an incomplete mask is wrongly flagged as an error. A PutFullData with mask 0111 would be accepted without d_error.

Check bit 35 of the 39/32 data-integrity encoder loses its inversion. Request data_intg then fails the device's check (spurious fatal alert) and response data_intg fails the wrapper's check (o_d_intg_err=1).
The line sits in the gen_rc branch, which is elaborated only for SwAccessRC. rv_timer has no RC fields, so the branch never exists and qs=q regardless.
Check bit 60 of the 64/57 encoder loses its inversion. Both the command integrity (request) and the response integrity (D channel) are then wrong, giving a spurious alert and o_d_intg_err.
The default (idle) alert_n becomes 0 together with alert_p=0, so the diff pair is no longer complementary. The receiver sees a signal-integrity error and o_alert_integ_fail goes high.
For RW/WO fields the write data select is inverted: a software write (we=1) stores the hardware value d, and a hardware update stores wd. Register read-back and the timer update break.
rd_req is true for non-Get opcodes. A Get is answered with AccessAck instead of AccessAckData, a Put is answered with AccessAckData, and re_o is wrong.
For a_size=2, mask_chk is forced to 0, so every 4-byte access is judged illegal and gets d_error=1. Full-word reads and writes to mapped registers fail.
The tick counter restarts at 0 on every cycle where it is not equal to the prescaler. For prescale>0 it stays at 0, so ticks never occur and mtime never advances. The tick period is wrong.
The sticky err_q is never set, so intg_err_o is asserted only while the corrupted request is on the bus. The fatal alert is no longer repeated until reset.

In the synchronous decoder this inverts the reset of diff_pq/level_q. The only effects are that diff_pq/level_q are held at 0 instead of tracking the input. rise_o/fall_o could matter only on the sender's ping pair, which stays constant (ping_req_i is tied to 0). level_q matters only during sigint, and every FSM output is overridden then. Nothing reaches a port.
outstanding_q is cleared on a_ack instead of set, so d_valid never rises. Accepted requests get no response.

The mask becomes (error_i && err_internal) || wr_req. For error reads, d_data now carries the register's read data instead of all-ones (for example a Get with a_size=3 to 0x110, or a Get to an unmapped offset). Only d_data differs, and no rule defines d_data on errors, so no requirement is broken.
The reset branch is taken when rst_ni=1, so tick_count is held at 0 during operation. For prescale>0 no tick is ever generated and mtime stays frozen.
The configuration checks run only when a_valid=0, so they stay at 0 whenever a request is valid. Every request is judged an error and gets d_error=1.
prim_flop is held in reset while rst_ni=1, so the alert sender and receiver flops stay at their reset values. The handshake never starts and no o_alert pulse occurs.
tick_count increments by 0 and stays at 0. For prescale>0 there is never a tick and mtime does not count.

The sender leaves AlertHsPhase2 while ack is still high instead of waiting for ack to deassert. The four-phase handshake is cut short and the repeat period of a fatal alert shrinks (6 cycles instead of 7), a visible o_alert timing change.
The rdata_q/error_q reset is inverted, so they are held at 0 during operation. All read data is 0 and d_error is never set.
data_o of prim_secded_inv_64_57_dec is left unconnected in every user (tlul_cmd_intg_chk, tlul_rsp_intg_chk). Only syndrome/err_o are used, and they do not depend on data_o.

The mutant makes addrmiss=1 when neither reg_re nor reg_we is active. error_i is only sampled when a request is accepted. In that case reg_re/reg_we is 1, unless err_internal is set, where the response is already an error with all-ones data. Write enables are also gated by reg_we, and the we-check enable also needs reg_we. No port changes.
The error tree uses OR instead of AND, so any single set write-enable bit counts as multi-hot. Each register write raises reg_we_err, giving spurious fatal alerts and o_alert pulses.
The interrupt output flop is held at 0 while rst_ni=1, so o_intr_timer_expired never asserts.
ping_rise becomes ping_req_d || !ping_req_q, which is constantly 1. The receiver issues pings and marks pending, so alerts are reported as ping responses and o_alert never pulses.
A handshake now needs alert_trigger AND ping_trigger. Pings never occur, so the sender never sends an alert.
The line is in gen_recov, which is elaborated only for IsFatal=0. rv_timer instantiates the sender with IsFatal=1, so the line does not exist in the design.
The register updates when wr_en is false and ignores real writes. Software writes are not stored, and idle registers load wr_data.
send_ping in the InitReq state only feeds ping_tog_pd, which is forced to 0 by send_init in the same state. The change has no effect.
data_o of prim_secded_inv_39_32_dec is left unconnected in tlul_data_integ_dec. Only err_o is used, and it depends on the syndrome, not on data_o.

The clamp only triggers on a sigint on the alert pair outside InitReq/InitAckWait. In this integration the only sigint is the deliberate one during the post-reset init sequence, where the receiver is in InitReq/InitAckWait and the clamp is skipped. No legal stimulus produces it, so integ_fail_o is always 0 either way.
ping_req_i is tied to 0 in the wrapper, so ping_rise and ping_pending_q are always 0. send_ping is 0 under both || and &&.
addrmiss is only evaluated when re AND we are both active, which never happens. Accesses to unmapped offsets no longer get d_error=1.

oh0_err and enable_err are both 0 unless the write-enable vector is multi-hot or a write enable fires without en_i. Both need an internal fault, because write enables require reg_we and an address hit. addr_err is off (AddrCheck=0). With oh0_err=enable_err=0, && and || give the same result.

mubi4_test_true_strict is inverted. In tlul_err every write with instr=0 is flagged as an instruction write and gets d_error. In the alert receiver init_trig_i=False now counts as true, so the receiver stays in init and no o_alert is reported.

A reset value of 1 for diff_pq in the sender's ping decoder creates a spurious fall event (ping_event=1) in the first cycle after reset. That cycle coincides with the receiver's init sigint on the ack pair, whose sigint_detected override sends the sender to Idle and clears ping_set_q. The receiver is in InitReq and ignores the stray alert level, so nothing is visible at the ports.
